classification.difficultyReason: Interpret combined transformations of absolute-value graphs, extract scale and translation from linear arguments, and solve both sign branches for intercepts when they exist.

content.prompt: Sketch the graph of each of the following functions. Label vertices and axial intercepts with their coordinates.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=|x|$ up 1 unit. The vertex is $(0,1)$.

At $x=0$, $y=|0|+1=1$. Since $|x|+1\ge1$, there are no $x$-intercepts. Draw the two rays with slopes $-1$ and $1$.

spec.description: Upward V with its vertex on the positive y-axis; no grid or numeric ticks.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=|x|$ right 2 units. The vertex is $(2,0)$.

At $x=0$, $y=|0-2|=2$. For an $x$-intercept, $|x-2|=0$, so $x=2$. Draw the two rays with slopes $-1$ and $1$.

spec.description: Upward V translated right; both axial intercepts labelled.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=|x|$ left 1 unit and down 1 unit. The vertex is $(-1,-1)$.

At $x=0$, $y=|1|-1=0$. For the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}|x+1|-1&=0\\|x+1|&=1\\x+1&=\pm1\\x&=-2\text{ or }0.\end{align*}$$
Draw the two rays with slopes $-1$ and $1$.

spec.description: Upward V with vertex below the x-axis and both zeroes labelled.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=|x|$ right 2 units and up 1 unit. The vertex is $(2,1)$.

At $x=0$, $y=|-2|+1=3$. Since $|x-2|+1\ge1$, there are no $x$-intercepts. Draw the two rays with slopes $-1$ and $1$.

spec.description: Upward V wholly above the x-axis.

answer.worked:
Reflect $y=|x|$ in the $x$-axis, then translate up 1 unit. The vertex is $(0,1)$.

At $x=0$, $y=1$. For the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}-|x|+1&=0\\|x|&=1\\x&=\pm1.\end{align*}$$
Draw the two rays with slopes $1$ and $-1$.

spec.description: Downward V with vertex and two x-intercepts labelled.

answer.worked:
Reflect $y=|x|$ in the $x$-axis and translate left 2 units. The vertex is $(-2,0)$.

At $x=0$, $y=-|2|=-2$. For an $x$-intercept, $|x+2|=0$, so $x=-2$. Draw the two rays with slopes $1$ and $-1$.

spec.description: Downward V touching the x-axis at x=-2.

answer.short: Vertex and $y$-intercept: $(0,-2)$. $x$-intercepts: $(-1,0)$ and $(1,0)$. Opens upwards; ray slopes $\pm2$.
answer.worked:
Since $|2x|=2|x|$, stretch $y=|x|$ vertically by factor 2 and translate down 2 units. The vertex is $(0,-2)$.

At $x=0$, $y=-2$. For the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}|2x|-2&=0\\|2x|&=2\\2x&=\pm2\\x&=\pm1.\end{align*}$$
Draw the two rays with slopes $-2$ and $2$.

spec.description: Narrow upward V with all intercepts labelled.

answer.short: Vertex and $y$-intercept: $(0,4)$. $x$-intercepts: $(-2,0)$ and $(2,0)$. Opens downwards; ray slopes $\pm2$.
answer.worked:
Stretch $y=|x|$ vertically by factor 2, reflect in the $x$-axis and translate up 4 units. The vertex is $(0,4)$.

At $x=0$, $y=4$. For the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}-|2x|+4&=0\\|2x|&=4\\2x&=\pm4\\x&=\pm2.\end{align*}$$
Draw the two rays with slopes $2$ and $-2$.

spec.description: Narrow downward V with vertex and both zeroes labelled.

At $x=0$, $y=|-2|+1=3$. Since $|x-2|+1\ge1$, there are no $x$-intercepts. Draw the two rays with slopes $-1$ and $1$.

answer.worked:
Translate $y=|x|$ left 2 units and down 2 units. The vertex is $(-2,-2)$.

At $x=0$, $y=|2|-2=0$. For the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}|x+2|-2&=0\\|x+2|&=2\\x+2&=\pm2\\x&=-4\text{ or }0.\end{align*}$$
Draw the two rays with slopes $-1$ and $1$.

spec.description: Upward V translated left and down.

answer.worked:
Reflect $y=|x|$ in the $x$-axis, then translate right 1 unit and up 3 units. The vertex is $(1,3)$.

At $x=0$, $y=-|-1|+3=2$. For the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}-|x-1|+3&=0\\|x-1|&=3\\x-1&=\pm3\\x&=-2\text{ or }4.\end{align*}$$
Draw the two rays with slopes $1$ and $-1$.

spec.description: Downward V with vertex and three distinct axial intercepts.

answer.worked:
Reflect $y=|x|$ in the $x$-axis, then translate left 2 units and up 3 units. The vertex is $(-2,3)$.

At $x=0$, $y=-|2|+3=1$. For the $x$-intercepts:
$$\begin{align*}-|x+2|+3&=0\\|x+2|&=3\\x+2&=\pm3\\x&=-5\text{ or }1.\end{align*}$$
Draw the two rays with slopes $1$ and $-1$.

spec.description: Downward V with vertex and all axial intercepts labelled.

answer.worked:
Since $|-u|=|u|$,
$$y=|-(x-1)|=|x-1|.$$
Translate $y=|x|$ right 1 unit. The vertex is $(1,0)$.

At $x=0$, $y=|1|=1$. For an $x$-intercept, $|x-1|=0$, so $x=1$. Draw the two rays with slopes $-1$ and $1$.

spec.description: Upward V; internal minus sign does not change absolute value.

answer.worked:
Since $|-u|=|u|$,
$$y=-|-(x+2)|=-|x+2|.$$
Reflect $y=|x|$ in the $x$-axis and translate left 2 units. The vertex is $(-2,0)$.

At $x=0$, $y=-|2|=-2$. For an $x$-intercept, $|x+2|=0$, so $x=-2$. Draw the two rays with slopes $1$ and $-1$.

spec.description: Downward V; internal minus sign leaves the absolute value unchanged.
